items.summary_original: A New York Times investigation revealed an alleged effort by operatives liked to Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee to recruit a second Dan Sullivan for Alaska’s ballot, but the report came as nearly 1 in 10 registered Alaska voters had already cast ballots. The timing means roughly 58,000 voters may have made their choices before learning of the reported effort that critics say was intended to create confusion with a same-name candidate. Peltola’s campaign and the DSCC have denied involvement. SENATE CONTROL IS A COIN FLIP — AND DEMOCRATS’ PATH RUNS THROUGH TRUMP COUNTRY Dan J. Sullivan made it to the four-candidate general election earlier this year after winning 2.5% of the vote in the primary. His campaign announcement did not list a party affiliation. His website does not state his position on any political issues. "Dan Sullivan challenges Dan Sullivan for U.S. Senate Seat, urges Alaskans to defeat incumbent, elect a Sullivan who stands up for Alaska," it read. The New York Times reported that the effort to recruit potential Republican spoiler candidates included Dan J. Sullivan. The effort spanned coordination between the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC) to Peltola staffers, according to text messages, interviews and internal documents. The FBI confirmed that federal and state agencies were conducting "court-authorized investigative activity" at multiple locations across Minnesota, including sites in the Twin Cities and Rochester, according to MPR News. Meanwhile, Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison's office also confirmed that its Medicaid Fraud Control Unit executed search warrants at Iska Inc. in St. Louis Park and Bright Horizon Therapy in Edina, both of which provide autism-related or other Medicaid-funded services. The operation involved the FBI, the Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General, IRS criminal investigators, U.S. Postal Inspectors and the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension, according to FOX 9 Minneapolis. items.summary_original: An election integrity expert raised concerns Wednesday about California and Washington after the Justice Department identified thousands of suspected noncitizen voter registrations, including cases in which residents told officials they were not U.S. citizens yet were still registered to vote. In an interview with Fox News Digital, J. Christian Adams, president of the Public Interest Legal Foundation, blamed the states’ automatic voter registration systems and local officials’ refusal to use available federal tools to verify citizenship. "Noncitizens are getting on the rolls all over the country through the motor voter program. They're going into (the) DMV. Sometimes they're even telling the DMV they’re not citizens, and states are still registering them to vote," Adams said. "That's why aliens are getting on the rolls in states like Washington and California that have automatic voter registration." FEDERAL OFFICIALS IDENTIFY 400 NONCITIZENS REGISTERED TO VOTE IN WASHINGTON STATE: 'TIP OF THE ICEBERG' California and Washington both require U.S. citizenship to register to vote, though their automatic voter registration systems differ. items.summary_original: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger’s effort to restore voting rights to tens of thousands of convicted felons sparked controversy Thursday after an attorney obtained an executive citation addressed to "Betty No Last Name," purportedly notifying the recipient that her voting rights had been restored. The citation identifies No Last Name as one of more than 66,000 Virginians whose rights to vote, serve on juries and seek public office have reportedly been restored under Spanberger's administration. The controversy comes ahead of a Nov. 3 ballot measure that would make voting rights restoration automatic upon release from prison. "It’s a big deal," said Virginia Beach attorney Tim Anderson, who first obtained the citation for No Last Name and shared it with Fox News Digital. SPANBERGER VOTING RIGHTS LETTERS SENT TO DEAD FELONS AMID BALLOT ACCESS PUSH "It’s clear [Spanberger] didn’t sign it. No governor and no secretary of the commonwealth would sign a restoration order that says Betty No Last Name, so they’re not looking at it; they didn’t review anything," Anderson told Fox News Digital in an interview Thursday. Each citation bears the signatures of the governor and Secretary of the Commonwealth Candi Mundon-King. "Whereas, Betty No Last Name, by reason of conviction(s), suffers political disabilities …," the citation obtained by Fox News Digital says. items.summary_original: In the American political scene dominated by the GOP-Democrat duopoly, Libertarians like Kentucky congressional candidate Jeremy Todd are looking to offer voters an alternative as they head to the polls during the midterm elections. "I think ultimately the Republican Party has abandoned… true conservatism, small government principles," Todd told Fox News Digital this week, asserting that "they may be more conservative than Democrats, but, to us true conservatives, that's not good enough." Todd, who views himself as "right of MAGA," mounted his long-shot U.S. House bid after Rep. Thomas Massie lost the Republican primary in Kentucky's 4th Congressional District to Trump-backed former Navy SEAL Ed Gallrein. Democratic congressional candidate Melissa Strange is also running in the contest. "We are welcoming people who are conservative, who believe in small, limited government, to my campaign and then to a larger movement that is probably gonna need to exist post the downfall of the Republican Party," Todd said. Former National Counterterrorism Center Director Joe Kent, who quit his post earlier this year due to his opposition to the Iran war, and former Rep. Ron Paul , have both backed Todd. items.summary_original: TEXAS — Gas prices are soaring ahead of the midterm elections, but President Donald Trump's supporters at campaign rallies in Texas say the rising costs aren't shaking their loyalty to the president, with some warning that the country's future is at stake. "I do experience that costs are high, but I'm in for the long haul and I support everything that he's been doing," one supporter told Fox News Digital at Trump's rally in Lubbock, Texas. Fox News Digital spoke with Trump supporters at rallies in Lubbock and Corpus Christi, two cities in a state deeply tied to America's oil and gas industry where voters acknowledged the economic squeeze but remained firmly behind the president. For some, concerns about the country's future and the rise of socialism are adding urgency to the approaching election. The national average for a gallon of regular gasoline stood at approximately $4.25 on Wednesday, up nearly 40% from roughly $3.05 a year earlier, according to AAA. items.summary_original: A little-known congressional maneuver could block members of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) from being sworn in as members of the House of Representatives next year, even if they win their elections on Tuesday. Members-elect must swear an oath to uphold the Constitution before they can become full members of the House. At the beginning of a new Congress, that oath is typically taken en masse by all 435 members, led by the House speaker. But an argument circulating in conservative circles posits that any member-elect can challenge another member-elect's right to be sworn in, provided they have compiled evidence that that person would not uphold their oath. That would then lead to House-wide deliberations followed by a vote on whether that member-elect has a right to be sworn in. In the case of DSA members, one potential argument could be the group's platform calling to scrap the current U.S. Constitution and draft a new one. Several DSA members and self-proclaimed democratic socialists have already won primaries across the country. SPEAKER JOHNSON REJECTS 'NONSENSE NARRATIVE' THAT GOP WILL REFUSE TO SEAT DEM WINNERS Rep. Keith Self, R-Texas, suggested to Fox News Digital that he could invoke the maneuver. "You cannot swear an oath to support and defend the Constitution while actively working to destroy it. The oath of office is not just words you say at a ceremony. It is a belief. It is an oath to our country and our fellow countrymen," Self told Fox News Digital.

items.summary: سناتور تد کروز، ایالت تگزاس، پیشنهاد کرد که در صورت انتخاب عبدالالسید، نامزد سنا، آمریکایی‌ها می‌توانند بمیرند، و این نشان می‌دهد که دموکرات‌ها می‌توانند از اطلاعات ایالات متحده برای اطلاع از تروریست‌ها استفاده کنند. "اگر عبدالالسید سناتور میشیگان شود، چاک شومر مطلقاً نمی‌تواند مانع از قرار دادن عبدالالسید در کمیته اطلاعات سنا شود. کمیته اطلاعات سنا به محفوظ‌ترین اسرار ما دسترسی دارد. و اگر درست بگویم که او حامی پرشور اخوان‌المسلمین است، در نتیجه این خطر وجود دارد که آمریکایی‌ها یک جنگ واقعی را به دنبال داشته باشند." ما در حال حاضر مردان و زنان نظامی آمریکایی را داریم که در حال مبارزه با تروریست های اخوان المسلمین هستند.
items.summary_original: Sen. Ted Cruz , R-Texas, suggested that Americans could die if Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is elected, suggesting that the Democrat could use U.S. intelligence to tip off terrorists. "If Abdul El-Sayed becomes the senator from Michigan , there is absolutely nothing to stop Chuck Schumer from placing Abdul El-Sayed on the Senate Intelligence Committee. The Senate Intelligence Committee has access to our most closely-guarded secrets. And if I am correct that he is a passionate supporter of the Muslim Brotherhood, there is a very real risk that Americans will die as a result," Cruz warned. "We have American service men and women in harm's way fighting Muslim Brotherhood terrorists right now. And we also have intelligence covert operatives heroically going undercover trying to anticipate and stop terror attacks before they happen, before they kill Americans. We have every reason to believe that Abdul El-Sayed, if he found out, 'OK, they're about to apprehend these terrorists,' that he would let those terrorists know," Cruz claimed . Speaking to Fox News chief political anchor Bret Baier last week, the Democratic candidate said that he has "never been" and "never will be a member of the Muslim Brotherhood." items.summary: دیوید او. کارتر، قاضی منطقه ای ایالات متحده، روز چهارشنبه درخواست اضطراری وزارت دادگستری برای وادار کردن کالیفرنیا به کنار گذاشتن برگه های رای پستی مربوط به بیش از 20000 رای دهنده ثبت نام شده که دولت ترامپ تابعیت آنها را زیر سوال برده است را رد کرد و حکم داد که مداخله در آخرین لحظه باعث اختلال در انتخاباتی می شود که از قبل در حال انجام است. بیش از 20000 رای دهنده که توسط مقامات وزارت دادگستری به عنوان "بیگانگان محتمل" شناسایی شدند، پس از تحقیقات امنیت داخلی و شرکای فدرال "از چندین روش غنی سازی داده ها و راستی آزمایی استفاده کردند" تا افراد غیرشهروندی احتمالی را در فهرست رای دهندگان کالیفرنیا علامت گذاری کنند. با این حال، مقامات کالیفرنیا با استناد به بررسی اولیه که افراد و رای دهندگان متولد آمریکا را بدون سابقه رای در میان آنها شناسایی کرده بود، صحت این لیست را رد کردند.
items.summary_original: U.S. District Judge David O. Carter on Wednesday rejected the Justice Department's emergency request to force California to set aside mail-in ballots associated with more than 20,000 registered voters whose citizenship the Trump administration has questioned, ruling that the last-minute intervention would disrupt an election already underway. The over 20,000 voters identified by Department of Justice officials as "likely aliens" were designated as such after Homeland Security Investigations and federal partners "used multiple data-enrichment and verification methods" to flag potential noncitizens on California’s voter rolls. California officials, however, disputed the list's accuracy, citing a preliminary review that identified U.S.-born individuals and voters with no voting history among those flagged. Carter, a Clinton appointee, ruled that the Justice Department's last-minute effort to intervene in California's election violated constitutional and federal-law constraints, while questioning the reliability of the government's evidence that the flagged voters were noncitizens. "The district court denied our emergency request to sequester ballots from 20,000 suspected noncitizens," First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital. items.summary: فاکس نیوز دیجیتال تایید کرده است که تحقیقات در مورد اینکه آیا ایلهان عمر، نماینده دموکرات، با برادرش در یک طرح کلاهبرداری مهاجرتی در سال 2009 ازدواج کرده است یا خیر، در سال 2016 در زمان باراک اوباما، رئیس جمهور سابق آمریکا، آغاز شد. یک منبع آگاه به فاکس نیوز دیجیتال گفت، یک دادستان ایالات متحده در مینه سوتا، که توسط جو بایدن، رئیس جمهور وقت آمریکا منصوب شد، در نهایت این تحقیقات را در سال 2021 تعطیل کرد. اکنون، این موضوع به عنوان بخشی از تحقیقات فدرال جدید در مورد این نماینده کنگره سومالیایی تبار، که بخشی از آن به این موضوع می‌پردازد که آیا او یا پدرش در درخواست او برای شهروندی شدن در ایالات متحده تقلب کرده‌اند یا خیر، دوباره مورد توجه قرار گرفته است. تاریخ مهاجرت ایلحان عمر، نماینده مجلس، به عنوان بازرسان فدرال احضاریه بستگان خود با بررسی های جدید مواجه شده است، منابعی قبلاً به فاکس نیوز دیجیتال گفته بودند که "نام واقعی" عمر ایلها است.
items.summary_original: The investigation into whether Rep. Ilhan Omar , D-Minn., married her brother in an alleged immigration fraud scheme in 2009 began under former President Barack Obama in 2016, Fox News Digital has confirmed. A U.S. Attorney in Minnesota, appointed by then-President Joe Biden, eventually shut down the probe in 2021, a source familiar with the matter told Fox News Digital. Now, the issue has been thrust back into the spotlight as part of a new federal investigation into the Somali-born congresswoman, part of which centers on whether she or her father committed immigration fraud on her application to become a U.S. citizen. REP ILHAN OMAR'S IMMIGRATION HISTORY FACES NEW SCRUTINY AS FEDERAL INVESTIGATORS SUBPOENA RELATIVES Sources previously told Fox News Digital that Omar's "real name" is Ilhan Nur Said Elmi. In a federal court document, she was called "Ilhan Omar Nur Said Elmi, a/k/a Ilhan Omar." In 2009, Omar, then a U.S. citizen, legally married a man with that surname, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi. The pair officially split in 2017. The New York Times first reported that Obama's FBI and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) began the probe in the summer of 2016, and that officials "found some evidence that [the marriage] was fraudulent." The Times reported that the investigation concluded when officials decided the potential felony crime was past the statute of limitations. items.summary_original: High-profile races that will determine which party controls the Senate for the next two years are extremely tight, according to a new CNN poll , as Maine and Kansas remain close and Democrats extended their leads in Texas and Michigan. Democrats, who are widely projected to win a majority in the House of Representatives, need to flip four Senate seats from red to blue in order to gain a 51-seat majority, protecting their majority from the vice presidential tiebreaker. In Maine, Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, is the only Republican incumbent running in a state that went for Kamala Harris in 2024. FOX NEWS POLL: NAIL-BITER IN MAINE SENATE RACE Collins' Democratic challenger is Troy Jackson, the former president of the state Senate who jumped into the race as a replacement for the previous nominee, scandal-plagued Graham Platner . The race has no clear frontrunner, according to the CNN poll, though Jackson holds a marginal lead. COLLINS INSISTS SOCIALIST RIVAL WON'T BEAT HER AS MAINE'S MONEY MACHINE: 'YOU'LL LOSE BIG TIME' Forty-nine percent of respondents told the outlet's pollsters they favored Jackson, compared to 45% for Collins. While Jackson is slightly ahead, at least 12.5% of voters say they could still change their minds. Respondents tied Collins to her party less than any other Republican running for Senate in the nation, with 46% of respondents saying they believe she would choose her constituents over the Republican Party. items.summary_original: Nearly 40 House Democrats appear to have shunned an effort by their colleagues to end the federal probe into Rep. Ilhan Omar , D-Minn. House Democrats led by Rep. Pramila Jayapal , D-Wash., sent a letter to the Trump administration earlier this week demanding a stop to the investigation into Omar's immigration paperwork, arguing it was a bid to sway her re-election campaign ahead of Tuesday's midterm Election Day. The letter was backed by some 175 House Democrats, more than two-thirds of the caucus — though some notable names were left off. Two of three of House Democrats' previous senior leadership did not sign the letter. Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi , D-Calif., and former House Majority Leader Steny Hoyer, D-Md., did not sign on. Rep. Jim Clyburn, D-S.C., who previously served as House majority whip, was among the signatories, along with all three current members of House Democratic leadership. 175 DEMOCRATS DEMAND TRUMP ADMIN STOP ILHAN OMAR INVESTIGATION, WARN IT COULD HURT HER RE-ELECTION BID Both Pelosi and Hoyer are retiring, but it's worth noting that nearing the exit did not stop other outgoing members like Rep. Nydia Velazquez, D-N.Y., from signing the letter. THE HITCHHIKER'S GUIDE TO WHY REMOVING ILHAN OMAR FROM CONGRESS COULD BE HARDER THAN TRUMP EXPECTS Democrats running in tight races also kept their distance from the public condemnation of the probe. Reps. Henry Cuellar, D-Texas, Tom Suozzi, D-N.Y., Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, D-Wash., and Don Davis, D-N.C.

items.summary: تل‌آویو، اسرائیل - ائتلاف دولتی بنیامین نتانیاهو، نخست‌وزیر رژیم صهیونیستی، روز پنجشنبه با اکثریت پارلمانی فاصله زیادی داشت، زیرا آرای تازه شمارش شده نشان دهنده افزایش چشمگیر حمایت از احزاب عربی بود که به طور بالقوه به مخالفان رای کافی برای به چالش کشیدن کنترل او بر پارلمان می‌داد. با شمارش 93.8 درصد آرا تا ساعت 4 صبح پنجشنبه به وقت محلی اسرائیل (10 صبح به وقت محلی در اسرائیل)، از جمله آرای حاصل از شمارش دو پاکت، پیش‌بینی می‌شود که جناح راست و مذهبی نتانیاهو 53 کرسی در کنست 120 عضوی اسرائیل به دست آورد، در حالی که 48 کرسی توسط اپوزیسیون سابق گاچینک‌دی به دست خواهد آمد. پیش بینی می شد که دو حزب عمدتاً عرب، مجموعاً 19 کرسی را به دست آورند و اکثریت پارلمانی بالقوه مخالف نتانیاهو را به 67 کرسی برساند.
items.summary_original: TEL AVIV, Israel - Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's governing coalition remained well short of a parliamentary majority Thursday as newly counted ballots showed a dramatic surge in support for Arab parties, potentially giving the opposition enough votes to challenge his control of parliament. With 93.8% of ballots counted as of 4 a.m. ET Thursday (10 a.m. local time in Israel), including votes from the double-envelope count, Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc was projected to win 53 seats in Israel's 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot. The two predominantly Arab parties were projected to secure a combined 19 seats, bringing the potential anti-Netanyahu parliamentary majority to 67. The updated figures showed Netanyahu's Likud remaining the largest individual party with 26 seats, followed by Eisenkot's Yashar party with 21 and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's Beyachad party with 12. The figures remain preliminary. NETANYAHU DEFIES EXIT POLLS AS VOTE SHIFTS IN HIS FAVOR, BUT MAJORITY REMAINS ELUSIVE The results leave neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot with the 61 seats required to form a government independently, raising the prospect of difficult coalition negotiations or another election. The biggest shift came from Israel's Arab voters, whose turnout surged compared with previous elections, potentially reshaping the country's political balance. items.summary_original: The fiance of Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich. has come out and said he cannot vote for Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed , believing he is an antisemite. Stevens, though, remains undaunted, backing the candidate for Senate. Jason Turkish, a Jewish registered Democrat, told The Detroit News he will be voting for Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers, appearing at a Rogers event sponsored by the Republican Jewish Coalition on Wednesday night at the Townsend Hotel in Birmingham, Michigan. "I waited, and I watched and I listened for Abdul to moderate – but he didn't moderate, he escalated," Turkish, a Michigan lawyer himself, told reporters on the sidelines of that event in a video published by The Detroit News. FORMER RIVAL DODGES FULL-THROATED EL-SAYED ENDORSEMENT AFTER BITTER SENATE PRIMARY "He's gotten worse, and worse and worse as this general election campaign has gone on. Rather than bringing people together, he's just driven them further and further apart." Despite Turkish's concerns, Stevens has not backed down from her support for the Democrat who defeated her in a closely fought primary this summer. HALEY STEVENS RIPPED BY FELLOW DEMS FOR REFUSING TO EXPLICITLY BACK EL-SAYED: 'STAY THE F--- OFF TELEVISION' "Like a lot of households across America, we're a house divided," Stevens told CNN. Sylvia is also accused of meeting journalists outside the Pentagon with the alleged intention of leaking classified material after Hegseth imposed new media restrictions requiring reporters to be escorted inside the building. HEGSETH ANNOUNCES JOINT TASK FORCE WITH DOJ TO PROSECUTE LEAKS TO JOURNALISTS 'WITH THE FULL FORCE OF THE LAW' Fox News Digital has reached out to Sylvia for comment but did not hear back at time of publication. The Justice Department declined to comment specifically on Sylvia but said it has "ongoing investigations related to possible leaks of classified information" and works closely with the Department of War. Pentagon chief spokesman Sean Parnell said the personnel action followed "an extensive Air Force OSI investigation," though he did not identify Sylvia by name in his statement or provide further details about the investigation. items.summary_original: Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil's presidential election to leftist incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Sunday, declared himself the country's leader after arriving in Florida on Wednesday. Bolsonaro fled his country after Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered his passports to be seized less than a day after Lula won the election. "I want to say, not only to my 60 million voters but to the Brazilian people, that I am the leader and that the criminals who stole Brazil’s election are part of a criminal organization that has established a tyranny," he said in an open letter posted on X. According to Reuters, Bolsonaro initially declared himself "the elected president" in a since-deleted post. He then sent out an updated letter on X, which included calling himself the rightful "leader" of Brazil. Bolsonaro, who lost the runoff election by a 3.58% margin, was served with an order to forfeit his passports and not to leave the country on Monday. "I was ordered right on the street to hand over my passports, and I'm also prohibited from leaving the country," Bolsonaro said, according to a Fox News Digital translation of a video he posted to his social media channels Monday. The order was signed by de Moraes, who Bolsonaro supporters accuse of being a staunch ally of Lula. items.summary_original: A federal judge rejected the Justice Department’s request for a temporary restraining order that would have barred California from counting mail ballots from more than 20,000 alleged noncitizen voters, saying the election "is already underway." U.S. District Judge David Carter, in a ruling issued late Wednesday night after a hearing in Los Angeles, said the government's request "would wreak havoc and disrupt the election that is already underway, create a chilling effect on election workers and voters alike, and discount the votes of United States citizens." The Justice Department immediately appealed the decision to the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals. CALIFORNIA MUST RESPOND TO DOJ'S EMERGENCY REQUEST OVER BALLOTS MAILED TO ALLEGED NONCITIZENS, COURT RULES "The district court denied our emergency request to sequester ballots from 20,000 suspected noncitizens," U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli wrote on X. "Every day, more ballots are processed by election officials. This ongoing emergency disenfranchises American citizens through dilution. The Solicitor General authorized an immediate appeal . We filed our Notice of Appeal and will immediately seek an emergency order from the Ninth Circuit." items.summary_original: The Justice Department's Antisemitism Task Force Chairman Leo Terrell is taking the Trump administration’s fight against antisemitism directly into Jewish communities on a 15-city nationwide tour, and he says he means business. Terrell told Fox News Digital that local leaders have too often failed to respond while Jewish Americans face threats in their schools, workplaces and houses of worship. "The whole purpose of this tour is to go to where the problem is at, to address their needs, and to provide them with federal support," Terrell said. "Antisemitism is now, and we have to come up with solutions for the future." ANTISEMITIC VIOLENCE REACHES DEADLIEST LEVEL SINCE 1994, NEW GLOBAL REPORT FINDS The "American Tour Against Hate" began Oct. 14 in Michigan, bringing representatives from the Justice Department , FBI and Labor Department together with Jewish residents, students, educators and religious leaders. The federal officials addressed antisemitism in workplaces and schools, as well as the enforcement of hate-crime laws. Terrell said the tour was created to reach communities that feel ignored or abandoned by local officials and to connect them directly with federal resources. "We had the FBI at the first tour meeting because some of these cities have failed to prosecute hate crimes," Terrell said, naming Los Angeles, Boston, San Francisco, New York and Detroit. items.summary_original: In the wake of a New York Times report detailing an alleged Democrat-linked election scheme by the campaign team of Rep. Mary Peltola that involved the recruitment of a candidate with nearly the exact same name as an incumbent GOP senator, Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy announced that he was ordering a probe into the matter. "Today’s New York Times reporting reveals disturbing new evidence of an organized effort to manipulate Alaska’s elections by recruiting candidates — including one with the same name as an incumbent U.S. Senator — to deliberately confuse voters and misdirect their votes. The Alaska Division of Elections investigated these very concerns in June of this year. The new reporting substantially supports the Division’s findings," Dunleavy noted in a post on X. MARY PELTOLA'S CAMPAIGN, DEMS BACKED COVERT SCHEME TO FIELD SPOILER CANDIDATES IN ALASKA SENATE RACE: REPORT "I am therefore directing the Department of Public Safety to investigate whether this scheme violated Alaska’s laws and whether criminal charges or civil action are warranted. The evidence will determine what happens next," the GOP governor continued . "Alaskans have a fundamental right to vote for the candidate they actually intend to support. Deliberately tricking voters into casting their ballots for someone else strikes at the integrity of our elections. Anyone or any organization found to have broken the law must be held accountable," he added. SEN DAN SULLIVAN BRANDS PELTOLA'S ALLEGED BALLOT SCHEME

items.summary_original: TEL AVIV, Israel: Israel's two Arab parties are in a position to have a say in who the country's next prime minister and government will be — but not if Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has anything to do with it, after he alleged serious criminal activities took place during voting in the Arab areas of the nation. The two parties were projected to win a combined 19 Knesset seats, according to preliminary results. With both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud-led right-wing bloc and the opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s centrist bloc falling short of the 61 seats needed for a parliamentary majority. On Wednesday, Prime Minister Netanyahu wrote on X that Israel’s election had been "stolen by Arab parties that support terrorism and the elimination of the Jewish state," alleging serious criminal offenses, including bribery, threats, violence, forgery and the use of prohibited software to mobilize voters. items.summary: یکی از جمهوری خواهان ارشد مجلس نمایندگان که تحقیقات درباره ActBlue را رهبری می کند، هشدار می دهد که پلت فرم اصلی جمع آوری کمک های مالی دموکرات ها ممکن است با اتهامات جنایی روبرو شود. برایان استیل، رئیس کمیته امور مجلس نمایندگان، برایان استیل، به فاکس نیوز دیجیتال گفت که تحقیقات کنگره در مورد ActBlue ادامه خواهد داشت و او مشکوک است که اگر دادستان های فدرال معتقد باشند که جرمی در دادگاه قابل اثبات است، وزارت دادگستری (DOJ) نیز اقدام خواهد کرد. استیل به فاکس نیوز دیجیتال گفت: "ما می دانیم که ActBlue استانداردهای پیشگیری از کلاهبرداری را که برای جلوگیری از راه یافتن وجوه خارجی از طریق پلتفرم ActBlue به کمپین های دموکراتیک و اهداف دموکراتیک ضروری بود، نداشت. من معتقدم که در نهایت باید این تحقیقات را ادامه دهیم." یکی دیگر از رهبران ACTBLUE خواهش کرد
items.summary_original: A top House Republican leading the investigation into ActBlue is warning that Democrats' main fundraising platform could potentially face criminal charges. Committee on House Administration Chairman Bryan Steil, R-Wis., told Fox News Digital that the congressional investigation into ActBlue would continue and that he suspected the Department of Justice (DOJ) would act as well if federal prosecutors believed a crime could be proven in court. "We know that ActBlue did not have the fraud prevention standards in place that were necessary to prevent foreign funds from finding their way, through the ActBlue platform, into Democratic campaigns and Democratic causes. I'm of the belief that we ultimately need to continue this investigation," Steil told Fox News Digital. ANOTHER ACTBLUE LEADER PLEADS FIFTH AS HOUSE INVESTIGATES ALLEGED FOREIGN DONATIONS "And then, separate of that, the United States Department of Justice will make a decision as to whether or not they believe that there was a crime committed. And if they can prove that in court, my belief would be that the Department of Justice would move forward." Steil's committee, along with the House committees on oversight and the judiciary, have for years probed allegations that ActBlue's lax verification standards have allowed foreign cash to seep into American elections. ActBlue has denied any wrongdoing and dismissed the probe as a partisan attack. DEM FUNDRAISING GIANT MAKES DAMNING ADMISSION AS GOP PROBES FOREIGN DONATION ALL

items.summary: حرکات آغازین جنگ بزرگ بعدی می تواند صدها مایل بالاتر از زمین آشکار شود. دشمنان ایالات متحده به دنبال راه هایی برای کور کردن نیروهای آمریکایی در درگیری های آینده از طریق ایجاد اختلال در ارتباطات، غیرفعال کردن GPS، استفاده از لیزر برای حمله به ماهواره ها یا از بین بردن کامل آنها هستند. ارزیابی جدید آژانس اطلاعات دفاعی نشان می‌دهد که چگونه چین و روسیه در حال توسعه راه‌های پیچیده برای مختل کردن یا نابود کردن ماهواره‌های ایالات متحده هستند. این شامل یک ماهواره روسی است که برای حمل سلاح هسته ای در مدار زمین طراحی شده است. نیروهای آمریکایی برای برقراری ارتباط در میدان‌های نبرد، هدایت کشتی‌ها و هواپیماها، ردیابی نیروهای دشمن، شناسایی پرتاب موشک و هدایت سلاح‌های دقیق به سمت اهداف خود به ماهواره‌ها متکی هستند. آفلاین کردن این سیستم‌ها می‌تواند باعث شود که نیروهایی برای دیدن، برقراری ارتباط و خیابان با مشکل مواجه شوند
items.summary_original: The opening moves of the next major war could unfold hundreds of miles above Earth. U.S. adversaries are looking at ways to blind American forces in future conflict by jamming communications, disabling GPS, using lasers to attack satellites or destroying them completely. A sweeping new Defense Intelligence Agency assessment details how China and Russia are developing sophisticated ways to disrupt or destroy U.S. satellites. This includes a Russian satellite designed to carry a nuclear weapon into Earth's orbit. American forces rely on satellites to communicate across battlefields, navigate ships and aircraft, track enemy forces, detect missile launches and guide precision weapons to their targets. Knocking those systems offline could leave forces below struggling to see, communicate and strike. AMERICA'S NEXT WAR COULD REACH US SOIL, TOP ARMY GENERAL WARNS "We can't do military operations the way that we do them today without satellites, without systems in space," Clayton Swope, deputy director of the Aerospace Security Project at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, previously told Fox News Digital. "Whoever has space and can deny that to their adversary has a huge asymmetric advantage in a conflict," Swope said. CHINA IS TAKING THE FIGHT TO THE STARS. John Nagel said it should be easy for the Somali-born congresswoman to clear up any public misunderstandings of her immigration status amid a federal investigation into alleged fraud and said that Omar views herself as Somali first, American second. He also claimed that Minneapolis has a "terrorist problem" and a gun-running operation, and called for a task force to crack down on the Somali gang violence. "We have two problems in Minnesota. We have a terrorist problem, which you saw with the Mall of America — thank God that the FBI actually took care of that before anybody got in there — and then we have a Somali gang problem," the career law enforcement officer told Fox News Digital. Nagel, who spent 30 years as a state trooper, claims the issue extends beyond Somali gangs, noting: "We have Somali gangs, we have Asian gangs, we have Black gangs, we have Latino gangs, and we need a gang task force." items.summary_original: FREMONT, Neb. — Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., likes to joke that he’ll be whatever his candidates need him to be in order to win their races. "I tell all of our candidates, I'll come out for you or against you, whichever helps you the most," Thune told Fox News Digital. Thune’s tongue-in-cheek response came just before he attended a roundtable in Nebraska alongside Sen. Pete Ricketts, R-Neb., who is running a tight race against independent Dan Osborn. That stop inside a corrugated metal building nestled among row after row of cornfields was among several visits the top Senate Republican has made across the country this cycle. Since the Senate left Washington, D.C., last month to hit the campaign trail, Thune has been busy, hitting key states like Georgia, South Carolina, Florida, Minnesota, Nebraska, Iowa and Ohio. But as Thune racks up miles on the road, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., has been largely absent. items.summary: تیم فوتبال لیورپول در مرحله یک‌هشتم‌نهایی ای‌اف‌ال کاپ پس از تساوی یک بر یک مقابل چلسی، در ضربات پنالتی ۶ بر ۵ پیروز شد و به یک‌چهارم نهایی رسید. مامارداشویلی پنالتی امگا را مهار کرد و فوفانا نیز آخرین پنالتی چلسی را از دست داد.

items.title: مای ساتو: حکومت ایران هیچ راه قانونی برای ابراز مخالفت باقی نگذاشته است
items.summary: مای ساتو، گزارشگر ویژه سازمان ملل در امور ایران، گفت محدودیت‌های قانونی و برخوردهای امنیتی حکومت، هیچ راه قانونی برای ابراز مخالفت باقی نگذاشته است. او تاکید کرد چهار دهه سرکوب، اعتراض‌ها را متوقف نکرده و تنها نارضایتی‌ها را عمیق‌تر کرده است.

items.title: جنوا ۲-۰ یوونتوس؛ ده‌روسی، بیانکونری را ۱۱ امتیاز از صدر دور کرد
items.summary: تیم فوتبال یوونتوس در هفته نهم سری آ با گل‌های اهیزیبوئه و بالدانزی، دو بر صفر مقابل جنوا شکست خورد و به رده هشتم سقوط کرد. تیم اسپالتی با سومین شکست فصل، اکنون ۱۱ امتیاز با صدر و شش امتیاز با رده چهارم فاصله دارد.

items.title: منچسترسیتی ۴ (۲-۲) ۳ برایتون؛ صعود سیتی به یک‌چهارم نهایی ای‌اف‌ال کاپ در ضربات پنالتی

"Kris Mayes thinks Arizona has too many golf courses. Instead of attacking an industry that contributes to our economy, the attorney general should be focused on enforcing the law, protecting consumers and defending Arizona families." items.title: انتخابات اسرائیل؛ چشم‌ها به انتخاب هرتسوگ: نتانیاهو یا آیزنکوت؟
items.summary: در‌حالی‌که تا دیشب تمام نگاه‌ها به بنیامین نتانیاهو و گادی آیزنکوت بود، اکنون چشم‌ها به اسحاق هرتسوگ دوخته شده است که ببینند رئیس‌جمهور چه کسی را مامور تشکیل دولت می‌کند؛ در حالی که او به‌روشنی گفته است که می‌خواهد به هر قیمت از تکرار انتخابات پرهیز کند. آقای هرتسوگ گفت که نتایج رسمی را هفته آینده دریافت خواهد کرد و پس از آن رایزنی‌ها آغاز خواهد شد اما «یک چیز باید روشن باشد و من این را پیش از انتخابات هم گفته‌ام، باید ما باید هر کاری از دستمان برمی‌آید انجام دهیم تا از یک انتخابات دیگر پرهیز کنیم.» او گفت: «بنابراین انتظار دارم هر کسی که به اینجا می‌آید، با ذهنی باز و پذیرا بیاید.»

items.summary_original: EXCLUSIVE: Two Republican members of Congress sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressing concern over the state of NATO ally Albania’s democratic backsliding, urging the department to use its visa restriction authority against Albanian officials complicit in significant corruption. "We write to express concern about the state of democracy and the rule of law in the Republic of Albania, a NATO ally and candidate for European Union membership. The United States has invested heavily in Albania's justice reforms and has a strong interest in their success. Recent events suggest that progress is fragile and, in key areas, at risk of reversal," the letter to Secretary Rubio said. items.summary: تصمیم دولت بریتانیا برای پذیرش اقدامات گسترده برای مقابله با یهودی ستیزی در مدارس، تضاد شدیدی با استراتژی اخیراً رونمایی شده شهردار نیویورک، زهران ممدانی، ایجاد می‌کند و این سؤال را ایجاد می‌کند که چرا طرح بریتانیا خاص‌تر از طرح پیشنهادی در یهودی‌نشین‌ترین شهر آمریکا به نظر می‌رسد. دولت بریتانیا تمامی 27 توصیه از یک بررسی مستقل در مورد یهودی ستیزی در مدارس و کالج های انگلستان را پذیرفت. این اقدامات شامل تشویق به تصویب تعریف کاری اتحاد بین المللی یادبود هولوکاست از یهودی ستیزی، آموزش تخصصی برای مربیان، تقویت روش های گزارش دهی و نظارت مستقل است. استراتژی 33 صفحه ای ممدانی - در حالی که فقط بر آموزش متمرکز نیست - در مقایسه، یک تعریف واحد از ضدها ارائه نمی کند.
items.summary_original: The British government’s decision to embrace sweeping measures addressing antisemitism in schools is drawing a sharp contrast with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s recently unveiled strategy, raising questions about why Britain’s plan appears more specific than the one proposed in America’s most Jewish city. The U.K. government accepted all 27 recommendations from an independent review into antisemitism in schools and colleges in England . The measures include encouraging adoption of the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance working definition of antisemitism, specialized training for educators, strengthened reporting procedures and independent oversight. Mamdani’s 33-page strategy — while not only focused on education — by comparison, does not adopt a single definition of antisemitism, explicitly address the relationship between anti-Zionism and antisemitism or establish numerical benchmarks for measuring whether its initiatives succeed. British Jewish author and Holocaust educator Dov Forman, who recently graduated from university, said Mamdani could learn from Britain’s targeted approach to addressing antisemitism in schools. MAMDANI PLEDGES MILLIONS TO COMBAT ANTISEMITISM WHILE LEAVING KEY QUESTION UNRESOLVED The British review followed a BBC report from Yavneh College, a Jewish secondary school near London, where students described how antisemitism has affected their daily lives. items.summary: به گفته مقامات صربستان، اندکی بعد از نیمه شب چهارشنبه، یک مهاجم مسلح به دو چاقو به یکی از اعضای ژاندارمری صربستان که از سفارت اسرائیل در بلگراد محافظت می کرد، حمله کرد که باعث شد این افسر برای دفاع از خود به فرد مهاجم شلیک کند. ضارب که خردسال بود، فریاد زد «الله اکبر» یا به زبان عربی «خدا اکبر» در حالی که صورت افسر را برید و افسر را کمی مجروح کرد. ایویکا داچیچ، وزیر کشور، گفت که مقامات این حادثه را یک حمله تروریستی می دانند و افزود که نیروهای امنیتی مهاجم را زیر نظر داشتند. داچیچ گفت که مهاجم از داعش حمایت می کند و پرچم سیاهی را که نماد این گروه تروریستی را در خود دارد در حساب اینستاگرام خود به نمایش گذاشته است. داچیچ افزود، گمان می رود مهاجم صربستانی و اهل شهر ساباچ باشد.
items.summary_original: An assailant armed with two knives attacked a member of Serbia's Gendarmerie guarding the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade shortly after midnight Wednesday, prompting the officer to fatally shoot the attacker in self-defense, according to Serbian authorities. The assailant, who was a minor, allegedly shouted "Allahu Akbar" — or "God is great" in Arabic — as he slashed the officer in the face, leaving the officer "slightly injured." Interior Minister Ivica Dacic said authorities are treating the incident as a terrorist attack, adding that security forces had been monitoring the assailant. Dacic said the attacker supported ISIS and displayed a black flag bearing the terrorist group's symbol on his Instagram account. The attacker was believed to be Serbian and from the town of Sabac, Dacic added. HALIMA SALMAN CONVICTED OF RECEIVING ISIS MILITARY TRAINING IN SYRIA, FACES 10 YEARS IN PRISON Israel's foreign ministry confirmed the " attempted terrorist attack ," and said the incident was under investigation by the relevant authorities. "The attacker was neutralized by local police. No embassy personnel were injured, and the mission was closed at the time of the incident, which occurred late at night," the statement said. According to Serbian prosecutors, an unidentified person wearing black clothes opened the door to the security booth outside the embassy around 12:15 a.m. local time. items.summary_original: Several Americans are believed to have been injured in a high-speed train collision that killed at least 68 people in Spain on Wednesday when one train collided with another that had stopped on the tracks. The crash took place in Spain's Castilla-La Mancha, with the regional government confirming the death toll and adding that another 58 people required medical treatment in hospitals. Several Americans are believed to have been hurt in the crash, according to the State Department. Rescue workers continue to search in the wreckage for survivors and bodies, with witnesses describing a gruesome scene. Wednesday's incident is the second high-speed rail crash Spain has suffered this year. Spain’s rail system operator ADIF said the crash occurred Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo. Both trains were carrying hundreds of passengers, and were headed in the same direction on a route from Madrid to Seville. CRASH INVOLVING SPEEDING TRAIN, MINIBUS IN BELGIUM LEAVES 4 DEAD INCLUDING 2 CHILDREN One train, run by the state-owned RENFE company, ran into the tail of the other train owned by private company IRYO that had stopped, knocking two of its cars off the track. Those companies were the same ones involved in January's crash. Esther Padilla, a spokesperson for the Castilla-La Mancha regional government, said 397 passengers were on the RENFE train and 147 passengers on the IRYO train. items.summary_original: TEL AVIV, Israel — Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's political bloc gained ground Wednesday morning as Israel counted votes from its first national election since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas massacre , but remained short of the majority needed to form a government, leaving the country facing another potential political deadlock. With approximately 70% of votes counted, Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc stood at 54 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, compared with 47 for the main opposition and 19 for Arab parties , according to partial election results reported by Israeli media. Netanyahu's Likud led with 27 seats, while former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party held 20. As both Netanyahu and Eisenkot claimed victory Tuesday night, Israelis told Fox News Digital that although they had expected a tight race, the shifting numbers and uncertainty over who could form a government had left many confused about what comes next. The results marked a shift from Tuesday night's initial exit polls, which prompted celebrations at Eisenkot's campaign headquarters in Tel Aviv. items.summary_original: TEL AVIV, Israel — Updated Israeli exit polls early Wednesday showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gaining ground against his political rivals but still falling short of a parliamentary majority, leaving the country facing a possible political deadlock despite a combined majority of seats projected for parties outside his governing bloc. An updated Channel 12 exit poll at 3:30 a.m. (Israel time) projected 53 seats for Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc, compared with 49 for the main opposition led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot and another 19 for Arab parties. Together, the opposition and Arab factions would hold 68 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, although they remain divided over forming a government together. Netanyahu struck a defiant tone in his first election-night speech at Likud headquarters in Jerusalem, declaring that his party had emerged as the largest in Israel and calling for the formation of a strong right-wing government. "Two things have become clear. The first is unequivocal: Likud is the largest party in Israel." "We do not have the final results yet, and many people will be surprised. Based on a stratified sample, it is clear that we have lost these elections . The Student List victory brings an end to 14 years of Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party rule, in what many are saying is the biggest political shake-up in the Balkans since the toppling of Yugoslav dictator Slobodan Milosevic in 2000. Observers say the Student List party's policies remain vague, which has some worried about Serbia's future. Ana Brnabic, vice president of the main Board of the Serbian Progressive Party, told Fox News Digital that, "The election victory of the Student List recalls similar electoral triumphs in other countries. The Student List represents a classical anti-establishment movement: it had neither a program nor a coherent political ideology. items.summary_original: TEL AVIV, ISRAEL — Campaign banners bearing the faces of Israel's political leaders cover buildings and roadsides, while in homes, coffee shops and family gatherings, the same question dominates conversations: Will Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu remain in power? With Israelis heading to the polls Tuesday, the country is bracing for a closely contested election that could end in another political deadlock. But this vote is unlike any other in Israel's recent history. For many Israelis, the election has become a referendum on accountability for the failures that allowed Hamas terrorists to carry out the Oct. 7, 2023, massacre — the deadliest attack in Israel's history. His government instead sought a politically appointed investigation, a proposal fiercely opposed by many bereaved families. Yet Israel's divisions began long before Oct. 7. In the months preceding the attacks, hundreds of thousands of Israelis took to the streets to protest Netanyahu's proposed judicial overhaul, which critics argued would undermine the country's democracy. items.summary_original: Former Colombian President Gustavo Petro has been accused of trapping and exploiting 48 women for presidential parties, with officials alleging they were hired "just to be with President Petro." Carlos Andrés Ríos, director of Colombia’s Administrative Department of the Presidency (DAPRE), claimed Petro oversaw a system that used service contracts to "systematically" control and weaponize the women , channeling public salaries in exchange for intimate relationships. "We are going to prove to the Colombian people how the Casa de Nariño was unfortunately set up, organized, and tailored for something completely different — not to govern, but to party there every single day, bring in women," Rios said during a congressional hearing last week. COLOMBIAN LAWMAKERS SEEK SUSPENSION OF TRUMP FOE GUSTAVO PETRO OVER ALLEGED MEDDLING IN UPCOMING ELECTION Petro issued a statement Sunday denying that he had used his public office to obtain sex. "I have never given out a contract in exchange for sexual relations . I would vomit on myself if I ever did such a thing," Petro said in a post on X. He argued that while his office provided state-funded aid programs for vulnerable women, he claimed that it is fundamentally different from giving contracts to individuals in exchange for sexual favors. items.summary_original: Ahead of Israel’s Oct. 27 national vote, President Donald Trump issued a sweeping endorsement of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s re-election bid, calling him a "great warrior," an "even greater partner for peace" and an ally in the confrontation with Iran. The backing could give Israel’s longest-serving prime minister a boost ahead of the country’s first national vote since the Hamas -led Oct. 7, 2023, massacre. The election is widely viewed in Israel as a referendum on whether to grant Netanyahu another term to pursue his war objectives, including disarming Hamas and Hezbollah and countering the nuclear threat from the Islamic Republic. In response, Netanyahu thanked Trump for his "extraordinary endorsement." "Together we will never let Iran’s regime get nuclear weapons ," he said. items.summary_original: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett is seeking a political comeback with an ambitious vision for the Middle East: expanding the Abraham Accords , building economic partnerships with Arab nations and rebuilding Israel's strained international relationships, particularly with the United States. For Bennett, whose American parents moved to Israel from San Francisco, the U.S. connection is both personal and political. The 54-year-old former technology entrepreneur, a familiar face on American television, believes his business background could help him work with President Donald Trump to advance regional diplomacy. "Naftali Bennett is the right leader to strengthen Israel’s global standing, including among the American people, thanks to his proven track record of working with world leaders and bringing people together, both as prime minister and as a successful businessman," Bennett’s campaign told Fox News Digital. "We are confident that our great friend in the White House, President Trump, and Israel’s allies around the world will welcome the opportunity to work with Bennett and the new government he intends to form. Together, we will revive the Negev Forum and expand the Abraham Accords, strengthening regional security and stability. That is why so many leaders across the Middle East and beyond who share a vision of a more secure, prosperous and stable region are eager to see Bennett lead Israel’s next government." items.summary: ارتش اسرائیل تمرینات نظامی گسترده داخلی را روز یکشنبه برای مقابله با نفوذهای مرزی غافلگیرکننده و حملات زمینی در شمال و مرکز اسرائیل آغاز کرد و لشکرهای متعدد و دارایی های هوایی را در بحبوحه افزایش تنش های منطقه ای بسیج کرد. این رزمایش که قرار است بیش از 48 ساعت ادامه داشته باشد، در حالی برگزار شد که یک کارشناس امنیتی اسرائیل به جنگ یوم کیپور در سال 1973 اشاره کرد، زمانی که مصر و سوریه از تمرین‌هایی برای پنهان کردن آمادگی برای حمله غافلگیرانه استفاده کردند و هشدار داد که تشدید تنش‌ها در منطقه در واقع می‌تواند عاملی باشد که او آن را "اشتباه محاسباتی خطرناک" توصیف کرد. به گفته ارتش اسرائیل، مانورهای گسترده شامل لشکر 210 فرماندهی شمالی، لشکر کرانه باختری، و لشکرهای 98 و 96 فرماندهی مرکزی، در کنار نیروی هوایی اسرائیل است. ایران ما را با جنگ روانی هدف قرار می دهد
items.summary_original: The Israeli military launched large-scale domestic military exercises on Sunday to counter surprise border infiltrations and ground raids across northern and central Israel, mobilizing multiple divisions and air assets amid rising regional tensions. The drills, set to continue over 48 hours, came as an Israeli security expert invoked the 1973 Yom Kippur War, when Egypt and Syria used exercises to disguise preparations for a surprise attack, warning that escalating tensions in the region could in fact trigger what he described as a "dangerous miscalculation." The large-scale maneuvers, the IDF said, involve the Northern Command’s 210th Division, the West Bank Division, and the Central Command’s 98th and 96th divisions, alongside the Israeli Air Force. IRAN TARGETS US WITH PSYCHOLOGICAL WARFARE CAMPAIGN TO MANIPULATE AMERICANS, EMBARRASS TRUMP: EXPERTS The exercise, scheduled just ahead of Israel's elections Oct. 27, aims to "maintain the forces’ alertness and readiness, strengthen the ability to defend communities, and make full use of aerial capabilities for defense in the area," according to the IDF. On Friday, the IDF said troops would practice "a variety of scenarios, including a surprise attack and infiltration into Israeli territory by air and land," incorporating lessons learned from the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks on Israel. items.summary_original: Incumbent leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated right-wing challenger Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro in Sunday's presidential second-round runoff, according to Brazil’s electoral court and The Associated Press. The deeply polarized nation returned to the polls for a second round of voting on Sunday. With 100% of the vote counted, Lula won 51.8% of the vote, defeating Bolsonaro by nearly 4.4 million votes. Despite trailing by nearly 4.4 million votes, Bolsonaro has refused to concede and has called for the election results to be annulled. Lula addressed supporters after winning re-election to a fourth, nonconsecutive term, expressing gratitude to the Brazilian people. "No one is required to like the president-elect, but he must govern for everyone," Lula said. Referring to his opponent, Lula said, "This was a defeat for denialism and lies." BRAZIL BECOMES NEXT TEST FOR LATIN AMERICA’S SURGING CONSERVATIVE MOVEMENT Lula’s victory followed confusion at polling places after Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin ordered a last-minute, two-hour extension of voting nationwide. The order came three minutes before polls were scheduled to close, and some polling places reportedly received word only after they had already closed. Both the Lula and Bolsonaro campaigns had requested that voting remain open longer, citing transportation problems and severe weather in different parts of the country. items.summary: سخنگوی سابق ولودیمیر زلنسکی، رئیس‌جمهور اوکراین، روز یکشنبه از او خواست تا با ولادیمیر پوتین، رئیس‌جمهور روسیه رو در رو در مسکو دیدار کند و استدلال کرد که روابط تجاری و سیاسی گذشته او در پایتخت روسیه از سال‌ها پیش می‌تواند به او در مذاکره برای توافق صلح در آنجا کمک کند. ایولیا مندل که از سال 2019 تا 2021 سخنگوی زلنسکی بود، به فاکس نیوز دیجیتال گفت که این کمدین سابق اولین میلیون ها دلار خود را نیز در روسیه به دست آورده است و شاید باید از این روابط برای دستیابی به صلح پایدار استفاده کند. مندل با بیان اینکه رئیس جمهور اوکراین افراد زیادی را از نخبگان پوتین می شناسد، گفت: زمانی که زلنسکی سرگرم کننده بود، اغلب در مسکو اجرا می کرد. او در واقع به طور حرفه ای در مسکو رشد کرد و اولین میلیون ها خود را در مسکو به دست آورد، و امروز وانمود می کند که هیچ چیزی ندارد.
items.summary_original: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's former spokesperson urged him Sunday to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin face-to-face in Moscow, arguing that his past business and political connections in the Russian capital from years back could help him negotiate a peace deal there. Iuliia Mendel , who served as Zelenskyy's spokesperson from 2019 to 2021, told Fox News Digital that the former comedian had also made his first millions in Russia and should perhaps leverage those ties to pursue lasting peace. "When Zelenskyy was an entertainer, he often performed in Moscow," Mendel said, adding that the Ukrainian president "knows a lot of people from Putin's elite." "He actually professionally grew in Moscow and earned his first millions in Moscow, and today he pretends that he has nothing in common with them," Mendel said. RECOVERING FROM LUNG SURGERY, POPE LEO URGES PUTIN TO AGREE TO CEASEFIRE IN RUSSIAN-HELD UKRAINE CITY "He needs to go to Moscow and needs to agree on compromises that are acceptable," she said, before adding that Zelenskyy "doesn't need to play his maximalist games and to play this noble actor." Mendel's criticism came as Ukraine , Russia and the United States prepared for another round of technical-level peace talks, potentially in Abu Dhabi or Switzerland, in November. items.summary_original: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado made returned to her home country on Sunday after nearly a year abroad, re-entering a political landscape transformed by the U.S. ouster of Nicolás Maduro . "I'm here. With you all," Machado wrote on social media, announcing her return for the first time since December. Her homecoming comes as Venezuela remains under the leadership of acting President Delcy Rodríguez, a longtime Maduro ally backed by the Trump administration, with no presidential election scheduled. President Donald Trump , asked about Machado's return by reporters in Port Huron, Michigan, said he was unaware of the development but expressed hope for her safety. TRUMP TOUTS ACCESS TO 65 BILLION BARRELS OF VENEZUELAN OIL IN DEAL HE SAYS WILL SLASH GAS PRICES "I don't know anything about it, but I think she's a very nice woman," Trump said. "She gave me her Nobel Prize. So how can I say anything else? And I hope she's safe. She's a very nice woman. But we're doing really well in Venezuela." Machado, who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2025 for her peaceful opposition to Maduro's government, did not disclose her exact location or provide details about how she returned. Fellow opposition leader Edmundo González, who ran for president in 2024 after Machado was barred from seeking office, confirmed her arrival on social media and said he would join her "very soon." items.summary_original: Polling ahead of Israel’s Oct. 27 election projects that National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir’s Otzma Yehudit Party will win between seven and ten seats in the 120-member Knesset, potentially making any future government led by Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud Party contingent on his support and positioning him to secure senior ministerial portfolios. His political rise mirrors a broader trend across Europe and the West, where parties such as Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella's National Rally in France, Geert Wilders’ Party for Freedom in the Netherlands, Australia's One Nation leader, Pauline Hanson, Italy’s Matteo Salvini and Germany's Alice Weidel of the AfD have all gained ground on traditional conservative political parties. The highly controversial Ben-Gvir, as national security minister, oversees the ministry responsible for internal security, including the Israel Police, Israel Prison Service and civilian firearms licensing. items.summary_original: From mass arrests in France to troop deployments in Italy, European leaders are taking varied approaches to protests and clashes across the continent. The unrest began in France in mid-September with student demonstrations over school conditions, then spread to other countries, where protests have centered on local grievances. President Donald Trump has used the unrest to press his hard-line immigration message, blaming France’s protests on immigration and urging the country to close its borders. PHOTOS SHOW AFTERMATH OF RIOTS AS MASKED GROUPS CLASH WITH POLICE ACROSS FRANCE French President Emmanuel Macron pushed back, calling foreign leaders' comments "unacceptable and even stupid" and accusing them of exploiting France’s crisis for political gain. Here’s how leaders across Europe are responding. Macron has vowed that those who loot or destroy property will be held accountable and made to pay for the damage. French authorities deployed 70,000 police officers nationwide Saturday as demonstrations took place in Paris and other cities. Some clashes broke out in several cities, including Paris, Lyon, Lille, Toulouse and Nantes. Police used tear gas, sound grenades and water cannons, and the Interior Ministry reported more than 1,300 arrests. items.title: بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی و پاسخ‌گویی؛ چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی بر این اصول ایستادگی می‌کند؟
items.summary: این مطلب توضیح می‌دهد که چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی در یکی از پرتنش‌ترین دوره‌های تاریخ معاصر ایران بر اصول بنیادین روزنامه‌نگاری، از جمله بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی، استقلال تحریریه و پاسخ‌گویی، پافشاری می‌کند. در این مقاله، با مرور شیوه تصمیم‌گیری‌های تحریریه، فرآیند راستی‌آزمایی اخبار، نحوه انتخاب مهمانان و برخورد با خطاها و انتقادها، تشریح می‌شود که هدف بی‌بی‌سی نه جانبداری از هیچ طرف، بلکه ارائه گزارشی دقیق، مستقل و مبتنی بر شواهد است تا مخاطبان بتوانند بر اساس اطلاعات قابل اعتماد، خود درباره رویدادها قضاوت کنند.

items.title: 'کودتای خزنده' در سپاه؛ نوار صوتی جلسه‌ای محرمانه در زمان جنگ
items.summary: با گذشت چهل سال از آغاز جنگ ایران و عراق، هنوز اطلاعات مرتبط با مقاطع مهمی از جنگ، از آرشیوهای محرمانه خارج نشده است. یکی از جلسات مهمی که در آن فرماندهی جنگ مورد انتقاد سپاهیان ناراضی قرار می‌گیرد، اوایل آذر ۶۳ برگزار می‌شود که در دهه‌های اخیر، رسانه‌های حکومتی ایران روایت‌های پراکنده و به‌شدت تحریف شده‌ای را از آن منتشر کرده‌اند.
